question: Which Article provides for the formation of Ward Committees in Municipal areas?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 243S**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 243S** of the **Constitution of India** provides for the formation of **Ward Committees** in Municipal areas.
 
• According to **Article 243S**, **Ward Committees** are mandatory for municipalities with a population of 3 lakh or more.
 
• These committees are formed to ensure **local representation** and to facilitate decentralized decision-making at the ward level. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• **Ward Committees** consist of members elected from the wards within the jurisdiction of the municipality and aim to represent the interests of the residents of those wards.
 
• The **Chairperson** of the municipality is also a member of the Ward Committee, providing a link between municipal governance and local governance.
 
• **Article 243S** emphasizes the importance of inclusive governance and ensures that the needs and concerns of smaller communities within municipal boundaries are addressed effectively.
 
• It is part of the **74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**, which aimed to strengthen urban local bodies in India. *Hence, the correct answer is Article 243S.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **74th Constitutional Amendment Act:**

 
 
• The **74th Amendment** introduced provisions for **urban local governance**, including the formation of municipalities and Ward Committees.
 
• It aims to provide a framework for decentralized governance and ensure **grassroots democracy** in urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Ward Committees:**
 
 
• These are formed at the ward level to **address local issues** such as sanitation, water supply, waste management, and public infrastructure.
 
• They act as an interface between citizens and the municipal administration, ensuring better **service delivery** and representation.
 
• **Example:** Ward Committees in cities like **Bangalore and Mumbai** play a critical role in urban governance.
 
 
 
• **Population Criteria:**
 
 
• Ward Committees are mandatory for municipalities with a population of **3 lakh or more**, ensuring their relevance in densely populated urban areas.
 
• In smaller municipalities, similar mechanisms may exist but are not mandated by Article 243S.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Decentralized Governance:**

 
 
• Ward Committees are an essential part of decentralized governance, enabling **citizen participation** in decision-making processes.
 
• They improve the efficiency of municipal governance by addressing local needs more effectively.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Implementation:**
 
 
• In many cities, Ward Committees face challenges such as **lack of funding, inadequate powers, and bureaucratic hurdles.**
 
• Strengthening the role and functions of Ward Committees can significantly improve **urban governance** and service delivery.
